story_type: spacecraft spins out of control after the first docking, emergency splashdown, 1966 mission film
hook: Docked in orbit, their spacecraft started to roll.
narration: Docked in orbit, their spacecraft started to roll, and it would not stop.
March 16th, 1966. Neil Armstrong and David Scott launched on Gemini 8.
They caught an Agena target rocket and made the first docking in space.
Then, seven hours after liftoff, the joined pair began to yaw and roll.
The crew shut down the Agena's controls. The trouble was not in the Agena.
Armstrong undocked. The spin got worse, building to about one turn every second.
[short pause] He fired the thrusters saved for reentry, and slowly took back control.
But those thrusters burn the fuel needed to get home. The fuel readings were too low, so the flight was cut short.
The destroyer Mason turned for an emergency zone in the Pacific, making thirty knots.
A search plane spotted the capsule under its parachute three miles away.
Rescue swimmers went into the water beside it.
outcome: The Mason took Armstrong, Scott and their spacecraft aboard, both in good shape.
title: Gemini 8 spun out of control
description:
On March 16, 1966, Gemini 8 made the first docking in space, then a stuck thruster sent Neil Armstrong and David Scott into a roll of about one turn per second. Armstrong regained control and the crew made an emergency splashdown in the Pacific, where the destroyer Mason picked them up. From the 1966 NASA film Gemini 8: This is Houston Flight.
